triggers.symptom: Siblings/in-laws fighting over dividends vs. reinvestment vs. family perks
triggers.action: Map each person to exact sector (Sector 7 = Family+Owner+Employee; Sector 4 = Family+Owner; Sector 5 = Family+Employee), then separate claims via Dividend + Employment Policies.

triggers.symptom: Rejects lucrative PE/acquisition offer to keep family name or board control
triggers.action: Cite Family Control & Influence + Identification with Firm; warn of long-term capital rationing / competitive obsolescence.

triggers.symptom: Heir has MBA/high skill but wants own startup instead of family firm
triggers.action: Separate ownership from management: transition heir to informed Board/Owner role and hire a professional CEO.

triggers.symptom: Majority sibling (55%) unilaterally sells core division without consulting sister
triggers.framework: Five Rights of Owners & Three Powers
triggers.action: Diagnose abuse of Power to Destroy + breach of Right to Inform / Define Value; fix via Shareholders' Agreement reserved matters.

triggers.symptom: 18 cousins in G3 argue at family dinners over jobs, cars, and dividends
triggers.framework: Family Council vs. Constitution vs. Board
triggers.action: Separate family deliberation (Council), moral entry/perk rules (Constitution), and corporate strategy/dividends (Board).

triggers.symptom: 72-year-old founder names successor twice but still signs every cheque
triggers.action: Diagnose identity fusion / fear of irrelevance; set binding handover calendar + move founder to Emeritus/Philanthropy role.

triggers.symptom: Non-family VP quits after unskilled son-in-law is hired at double pay
triggers.action: Enforce 3-5 yrs external work experience, real vacancy + independent evaluation, and market-benchmarked KPI pay.

triggers.symptom: Rich capital and fast decisions, yet fewer new products than rivals
triggers.action: High ability (patient capital) vs. low willingness (SEW loss aversion); fix via ring-fenced R&D / corporate venture unit.

triggers.symptom: Returning NextGen heir immediately fires loyalists and disrupts culture
triggers.framework: Anand Group: Earning the Right to Change
triggers.action: Sequence: Listen & learn operations -> win a bounded pilot project -> earn legitimacy -> modernize with trusted insiders.

triggers.symptom: Branch ignored Family Constitution in a dispute and sued in court
triggers.action: Translate transfer, ROFR, valuation, and reserved-matter rules from the non-binding Constitution into a binding SHA + Articles.

modules.title: M1: Foundations, Theories & India
modules.summary: Why family firms outperform or fail: Agency vs. Stewardship, SEW (FIBER), RBV Familiness, and Indian business history.

nodes.label: Alignment vs. Entrenchment (Inverted-U)
nodes.short: Low Type I agency (Stewardship) vs. high Type II (Principal-Principal) risk.
bullets: Anderson & Reeb (2003): Family firms outperform on average via long horizons + Alignment.
Type I (Owner-Manager) is low; Type II (Controlling Family vs. Minority) rises with unchecked power.
Entrenchment occurs when founders block succession, hoard cash, or extract private RPTs.
nodes.trap: Never claim family firms have 'zero agency costs'—Type II conflicts replace Type I.

nodes.label: SEW Theory (FIBER Dimensions)
nodes.short: Non-financial utility often overrides pure NPV/profit maximization.
bullets: F: Family control & influence. I: Identification of family with firm.
B: Binding social ties. E: Emotional attachment. R: Renewal of family bonds.
Explains debt aversion, PE rejection, and Crisis Resilience (Survivability Capital).
nodes.trap: SEW is double-edged: protects workforce loyalty in crises, but blocks needed capital/R&D.

nodes.label: RBV 'Familiness' & TCE
nodes.short: Idiosyncratic human, social, patient, and survivability capital.
bullets: VRIO Familiness: hard-to-imitate trust, speed, and patient financial capital.
Constrictive Familiness: insularity, nepotism, and resistance to outside talent.
TCE: Kinship/community trust (e.g., Marwari/Chettiar Hundi networks) cuts contracting costs.

nodes.label: Managing Agency (1970) -> Pyramids
nodes.short: How Indian groups evolved from License Raj to post-1991 global competition.
bullets: Managing Agency System allowed sweeping control on small equity; abolished in 1970.
License Raj rewarded bureaucratic navigation ('active adaptation'); 1991 forced global quality ('proactive').

modules.title: M2: Three-Circle, Rights & Stages
modules.summary: Diagnosing role overlaps, ownership rights/powers, and generational drift from G1 to G3.

nodes.label: Three-Circle Model (7 Sectors)
nodes.short: Family, Ownership, and Business overlap creates competing claims.
bullets: Sector 1: Family only. Sector 4: Family+Owner (wants dividends). Sector 5: Family+Employee (no shares).
Sector 7: Family+Owner+Employee (founder/active sibling seeking reinvestment + control).
Rule: Separate employment pay from ownership dividends and family care.
nodes.trap: A spouse working in HR with 0% equity is Sector 5 (Family+Employee), NOT Sector 1.

nodes.label: 5 Rights & 3 Powers of Owners
nodes.short: Balance Power to Create/Sustain against Power to Destroy.
bullets: 5 Rights: Design (structures), Decide (strategy/board), Define Value (purpose/risk), Inform (reporting), Transfer (exit).
Power to Destroy = unilateral 51% dominance, blocking capital, or weaponizing vetoes.

nodes.label: G1 Owner -> G2 Siblings -> G3 Cousins
nodes.short: Complexity jumps as shared household memory fades across branches.
bullets: G1 Controlling Owner: key-person dependency & succession planning.
G2 Sibling Partnership: horizontal consensus without parent-referee.
G3 Cousin Consortium (Cousin Matrix): Active vs. Passive owner dividend clash + branch coalitions.

modules.title: M3: Succession & Handover
modules.summary: Beating the Three-Generation Rule through process, readiness tests, and separating Ownership from Management.

nodes.label: Three-Gen Rule & Dual Transfer
nodes.short: Separate Management Transfer from Ownership Transfer.
bullets: Shirtsleeves to shirtsleeves in 3 generations: dilution + entitlement + rigidity.
Management Transfer = operational CEO role (meritocratic). Ownership Transfer = equity/voting (trusts/SHA).
All heirs need Ownership Literacy (reading P&L/board decks), even passive ones.

nodes.label: Willingness x Ability Matrix
nodes.short: Match each successor quadrant to the right path.
bullets: High Will + High Ability -> Groom via external experience + P&L ownership.
Low Will + High Ability -> Active Board Owner + Professional Non-Family CEO.
High Will + Low Ability -> Structured mentoring + pair with strong COO; defer CEO.
nodes.trap: Never force a Competent-but-Unwilling heir into daily CEO operations.

nodes.label: Incumbent's Dilemma & Credibility Tests
nodes.short: Manage founder identity exit + NextGen external/internal tests.
bullets: Incumbent fears irrelevance -> shadow leadership overturns successor.
Fix: Binding handover calendar + dignified Emeritus/Chairman/Foundation role.
Paths: Crown Prince (1 heir) vs. Horse Race (parallel P&L) vs. Regency (interim outsider).

modules.title: M4: Family Dynamics & Conflict
modules.summary: Employment charters, equality vs. equity, women leadership, RPTs, and containing conflict.

nodes.label: Employment Policy, Equality vs. Equity
nodes.short: Equal ownership inheritance; equitable (market) executive pay.
bullets: 3 Policy Pillars: 3-5 yrs outside work, real vacancy + merit review, market-benchmarked KPI pay.
Prevents non-family talent flight ('glass ceiling') and abusive off-market RPTs.

nodes.label: Women Leadership & Working Couples
nodes.short: Move women from 'Invisible Force' to formal meritocratic succession.
bullets: Barriers: Primogeniture/patrilineal bias + stakeholder stereotyping.
CEO's Spouse & Working Couples: prevent home/office spillover via distinct functional domains.

nodes.label: Task -> Process -> Relationship Conflict
nodes.short: Keep strategic debate constructive; block escalation into personal war.
bullets: Task Conflict (what strategy?) = healthy if bounded by ROI data.
Process Conflict (budgets/roles) -> Relationship Conflict (personal hostility) destroys trust.

modules.title: M5 & M6: Pro-Management & Governance
modules.summary: Professionalisation without losing familiness, Board roles, and wealth/ownership vehicles.

nodes.label: Professionalisation & Innovation Paradox
nodes.short: Structural systems (KPIs/ERP) + Bridge Executive; ring-fence Exploration.
bullets: 'Be like an MNC' fallacy destroys patient capital and speed; separate Structural vs. Managerial prof.
Innovation Paradox: High Ability vs. Low Willingness -> ring-fence corporate ventures.
Internationalisation: Slow Uppsala entry protects SEW; once in, patient capital + diaspora trust win.

nodes.label: Board: Control / Service / Resource
nodes.short: Independent directors counter groupthink and open global networks.
bullets: Control (oversight/RPTs/NRC), Service (strategic counsel), Resource Provisioning (legitimacy/networks).
Firms resist independents over privacy and RPT scrutiny.

nodes.label: Council / Constitution / SHA / Office / Trust
nodes.short: Match the exact legal or family institution to the problem.
bullets: Family Assembly (all kin) vs. Council (elected reps) vs. Constitution (moral charter).
Shareholders' Agreement + Articles = legally enforceable (ROFR, drag-along, buy-sell).
Holding Co (voting unity) vs. Trust (estate/succession) vs. Family Office (liquid wealth) vs. Family Bank (branch buyouts/NextGen).
nodes.trap: A Family Constitution is NOT legally binding in corporate court without a matching SHA.

modules.title: M7 & M8: Impact, Anand & Institutions
modules.summary: Dual wealth optimization, Anand Group NextGen playbook, and Scott/North institutional shift.

nodes.label: Dual Wealth, Section 8 & Anand Case
nodes.short: Philanthropy builds NextGen cohesion; NextGen must earn the right to change.
bullets: Dual Wealth Optimization: financial resilience + measurable impact (Section 8 Co for CSR governance).
Anand Story: Returning heirs must listen -> prove wins on bounded unit -> modernize with loyalists.

nodes.label: Voids, Scott's 3 Pillars & Trust -> Rules
nodes.short: Why Indian conglomerates grew in voids and must now codify governance.
bullets: Institutional Voids gave conglomerates internal capital/talent advantage.
Scott: Regulative (SEBI/RPTs), Normative (ESG/peers), Cultural-Cognitive (norms).
North: Formal rules fail if they ignore Informal filial deference -> harmonize both.

traps.trap: Placing an in-law employee with 0% equity in Sector 1
traps.fix: They belong in Sector 5 (Family + Employee), not Sector 1 (Family only).

traps.trap: Treating a Family Constitution as court-enforceable
traps.fix: Only a Shareholders' Agreement mirrored in Articles of Association binds share transfers legally.

traps.trap: Confusing Family Office with Holding Company
traps.fix: Holding Co consolidates operating voting control; Family Office manages liquid family wealth/tax.
Distinguish Structural professionalisation (KPIs, ERP, boards) from Managerial (outside hires).

traps.trap: Saying family firms have zero agency problems
traps.fix: Type I (Owner-Manager) drops, but Type II (Majority Family vs. Minority) rises.
Ownership shares can be equal, while executive pay must be equitable (market/KPI-based).
Task conflict improves strategy until poor governance lets it spill into Relationship conflict.

traps.trap: Forcing a Competent-but-Unwilling heir into CEO
traps.fix: Separate ownership from management: keep them on the Board and hire a professional CEO.
